title: Minimum Insertion Steps to Make a String Palindrome
summary: Given a string, determine the least number of insertions needed to transform it into a palindrome.
statement: Given a string, determine the least number of insertions needed to transform it into a palindrome. A palindrome reads identically forwards and backwards.
constraints: s is a nonempty lowercase string.
Insert characters anywhere without deleting or reordering existing characters.
Return the minimum insertions needed to make the complete string a palindrome.
hints: Matching ends can surround an optimal solution for the inside substring at no extra cost.
For mismatched ends, insert a copy of either end and pay one plus the cheaper remaining interval.
Fill intervals from shorter to longer using dp[left][right].
The two cases exhaust the first and last characters of every target palindrome.
editorial: For matching endpoints, no insertion is required there and the inside interval determines the cost. For a mismatch, the target palindrome must pair either endpoint with an inserted copy, leaving one of two shorter intervals; choose the cheaper and add one. The oracle independently finds the longest palindromic subsequence by enumerating subsequences, and n minus that length equals the required insertions.

tests.explanation: The input is already a palindrome, so zero insertions are needed.
Two insertions can produce a palindrome such as mbdadbm.
